plan: With a private value of $27, I want to maximize potential profit. Since values are drawn independently and randomly, I'll use a strategic bid near my value. My goal is to win only if I can do so profitably. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances, but not so high that I risk negative profit. A bid around $30-$35 seems optimal - high enough to have a good winning probability, but not so high that I'll lose money if I win.

With a private value of $31, I want to maximize potential profit. Since values are drawn randomly between $0-$49, other bidders likely have similar incentives. A good strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer. If I bid too high, I risk paying more than my value. If I bid too low, I might lose. I'll aim to bid around $28-$30 to balance winning probability with profit margin.

My private value is $20. In a first-price sealed bid auction with three bidders, I want to bid strategically. Since values are randomly drawn between $0-$49, I'll aim to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. A bid around $15-$18 gives me buffer against overpaying. I'll assume other bidders might also bid somewhat conservatively, not wanting to risk significant losses. My goal is to win if possible while minimizing my payment.
